title: Etale covers over an integral morphism admit disjoint open refinements locally on the base
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be an integral morphism of schemes [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Let $V\to Y$ be an object of the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], let $v\in V$, and let $\{U_i\to X\times_Y V\}_{i\in I}$ be an etale covering family (the maps are etale and jointly surjective). Fibre products are those of [def-pc-fibre-product]. There exist an etale morphism $a:V'\to V$, a point $v'\in V'$ with $a(v')=v$, a set $J$, pairwise disjoint open subschemes $W_j\subseteq X\times_Y V'$ [def-weil-open-immersion] whose union is all of $X\times_Y V'$, a function $\alpha:J\to I$, and morphisms $b_j:W_j\to U_{\alpha(j)}$ such that the composite $W_j\xrightarrow{b_j}U_{\alpha(j)}\to X\times_Y V$ is the restriction of $\operatorname{id}_X\times a$. The empty decomposition is allowed when $X\times_Y V'$ is empty.

source.place: Tag 04DR (lemma-integral-B), proof: the disjoint decomposition asserted at the beginning, reduced to lemma-finite-B; Tag 04DP (lemma-simplify-B), displayed explicit refinement condition

proof.text: Choose an affine open V_0 containing v by the affine-opens basis. Replace the base by V_0 and the total space by T=X times_Y V_0. The base-change lemma makes T→V_0 integral; hence T=Spec(B) for V_0=Spec(A) and an integral A-algebra B, by the definition of integral. Pull back the given cover to T using covering base change. A neighbourhood over V_0 and maps into this pulled-back cover give the required neighbourhood over V and maps into the original cover by composition. If T is empty, take V′=V_0 and J empty.

For every point of each covering member over T choose an affine open neighbourhood, then a principal open on which the etale algebra over B is standard, using the affine-opens basis and the locally-standard lemma. These refined members still cover T. Their images are open by the etale open-map lemma; since Spec(B) is quasi-compact, finitely many images cover T. Denote the chosen members by E_k=Spec(P_k.Ring), k in a finite set K, and retain their maps E_k→U_{i(k)} times_V V_0. This is a refinement, not a replacement without maps to the original cover.

source.place: Tag 04DR (lemma-integral-B), standard etale covering reduction; Algebra Tag 00UE (proposition-etale-locally-standard)

proof.text: Apply standard-etale finite-subalgebra descent to the integral A-algebra B (the ring of T, not the ring of the original X). Obtain B_0⊆B finite over A and Q_k with B tensor_{B_0} Q_k.Ring ≅ P_k.Ring. Put Z=Spec(B_0) and F_k=Spec(Q_k.Ring). Then Z→V_0 is finite and the E_k are the pullbacks of F_k→Z. For the affine tensor-product identification, maps from any affine test scheme into the proposed pullback are compatible ring maps; the tensor-product universal property gives exactly these maps. The affine identifications glue on affine open covers of a test scheme, so they give the scheme fibre-product identification. The inclusion B_0→B is injective and integral: a monic equation over A for an element of B is also one over B_0. Lying over therefore makes T→Z surjective. For any z∈Z choose t∈T over z and an E_k-point over t; its projection to F_k lies over z. Thus {F_k→Z} is an etale covering, so the finite problem really is a covering problem.

Choose an algebraic closure Ω of κ(v) and its geometric point y of V_0. The Ω-fibre of Z→V_0 is finite: on affine charts tensoring a finite set of module generators keeps the algebra finite over Ω, and the finite-fibres lemma applies. For a prime of this finite-dimensional Ω-algebra, its quotient is a finite-dimensional domain. Multiplication by a nonzero element is injective and hence surjective, so that quotient is a field and already the residue field. It is algebraic over Ω and therefore equal to Ω; hence its points are precisely the finite set H of geometric points t:Spec(Ω)→Z over y. For each t∈H, the geometric-cover-lift lemma gives k(t) and a marked lift into F_{k(t)}. Apply the finite pointed-piece refinement to Z→V_0 and this pointed etale neighbourhood of t. Obtain a pointed neighbourhood c_t of y and its selected clopen piece D_t mapping over Z to F_{k(t)}. Its geometric fibre contains t and no other element of H: the other marked points lie in the other pieces of the disjoint decomposition.

source.place: Tag 04DQ (lemma-finite-B), finite fibre and pointed neighbourhood refinements

proof.text: Take the finite fibre product c of the c_t over V_0, with marked point given by the tuple of their Ω-points; for H empty use the identity neighbourhood. The small etale site has finite limits, so c is etale over V_0. Pull each D_t back to Z times_{V_0} c and compose its map to F_{k(t)}. In an ordering of H, set E_t=D_t minus the union of earlier D_s. Finite unions and differences of clopen subsets are clopen. These E_t are pairwise disjoint, have the same union as the D_t, retain their respective marked points because D_s excludes t for s≠t, and retain maps to F_{k(t)} by restriction.

source.place: Tag 04DQ (lemma-finite-B), finitely many refinements and disjoint pieces

proof.text: Let c_0 be the ordinary point underlying the chosen Ω-point of c. Every point of Z times_{V_0} c over c_0 lifts to an Ω-point over that marked point by finite geometric-point lifting. Its projection to Z is some t∈H, so it belongs to D_t and thus to the union of the E_t. Consequently the clopen complement R has empty fibre over c_0. The projection Z times_{V_0} c→c is finite (tensoring module generators proves this on affine charts); the finite closed-map lemma makes the image of R closed and excludes c_0. Restrict c to its open complement V′. Now the restricted E_t cover Z times_{V_0} V′ and remain disjoint with the same maps. This also handles H empty: remove the closed image of the entire finite scheme to obtain an empty pullback.

source.place: Tag 04DQ (lemma-finite-B), removal of the finite closed complement

proof.text: Pull each E_t back along T times_{V_0} V′→Z times_{V_0} V′ to obtain W_t. Inverse images commute with union and intersection, so the W_t are disjoint opens covering T times_{V_0} V′=X times_Y V′. The two compatible maps W_t→T and W_t→F_{k(t)} give, by the fibre-product universal property, a map W_t→T times_Z F_{k(t)}=Spec(B tensor_{B_0} Q_{k(t)}.Ring)≅E_{k(t)}. Compose with the retained refinement map to U_{i(k(t))}. Its map to X times_Y V is the original pullback projection because both components of the fibre-product map have those structural maps. Set J=H and α(t)=i(k(t)); if the total pullback is empty instead take J empty.
